extracted.intended_audience: employers, legal counsel, compliance officers, and other persons subject to the FTC Non‑Compete Clause Rule
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and complying with the FTC's Non‑Compete Clause Rule (Part 910) requirements on entering, enforcing, and notifying workers about non‑compete clauses, and the rule's exceptions, relation to state law, severability, and effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair method of competition — workers other than senior executives
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a worker other than a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person: (i) To enter into or attempt to enter into a non‑compete clause; (ii) To enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause; or (iii) To represent that the worker is subject to a non‑compete clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the §910.2(a)(1) prohibition; applies to entering, enforcing, or representing non‑competes for non‑senior‑executive workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair method of competition — senior executives
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a senior executive, it is an unfair method of competition for a person: (i) To enter into or attempt to enter into a non‑compete clause; (ii) To enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause entered into after the effective date; or (iii) To represent that the senior executive is subject to a non‑compete clause, where the non‑compete clause was entered into after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(a)(2); the rule treats senior executives differently by limiting enforcement/representations only for non‑competes entered after the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for existing non‑compete clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: For each existing non‑compete clause that it is an unfair method of competition to enforce or attempt to enforce under §910.2(a)(1)(ii), the person who entered into the non‑compete clause with the worker must provide clear and conspicuous notice to the worker by the effective date that the worker's non‑compete clause will not be, and cannot legally be, enforced against the worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(b)(1); applies to existing non‑competes covered by the prohibition and requires notice by the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must: (i) Identify the person who entered into the non‑compete clause with the worker; and (ii) Be on paper delivered by hand to the worker, or by mail at the worker's last known personal street address, or by email at an email address belonging to the worker (including current work or last known personal email), or by text message at a mobile telephone number belonging to the worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(b)(2); specifies required content and acceptable delivery methods for the required notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to notice when no contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person required to provide notice has no record of a street address, email address, or mobile telephone number for the worker, that person is exempt from the notice requirement with respect to that worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(b)(3); provides an exception to the notice obligation where no contact information exists in the person's records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model language constitutes notice
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §910.2(b)(1), the Commission's model language in §910.2(b)(4) constitutes notice to the worker that the worker's non‑compete clause cannot legally be enforced and will not be enforced against the worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model language is provided in the rule (Figure 1 to paragraph (b)(4)); using it satisfies the content requirement for the required notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for notice compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A person complies with the requirement in §910.2(b)(1) if the person provides notice to a worker pursuant to §910.2(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(b)(5); expressly creates a safe harbor for using the model language to meet the notice obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional notice in additional languages
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to providing the notice required in §910.2(b)(1) in English, a person is permitted to provide such notice in one or more languages other than English or to include internet links to translations; if providing optional notice, a person may use any Commission‑provided translation of the model language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.2(b)(6); allows multilingual notices and use of Commission translations but does not make them mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — bona fide sales of business
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of this part do not apply to a non‑compete clause that is entered into by a person pursuant to a bona fide sale of a business entity, of the person's ownership interest in a business entity, or of all or substantially all of a business entity's operating assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.3(a); exempts non‑competes that are part of bona fide business sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — existing causes of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of this part do not apply where a cause of action related to a non‑compete clause accrued prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.3(b); protects pre‑existing causes of action that arose before the rule's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — good‑faith belief of inapplicability
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not an unfair method of competition to enforce or attempt to enforce a non‑compete clause or to make representations about a non‑compete clause where a person has a good‑faith basis to believe that this part is inapplicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.3(c); provides a defense where a party reasonably and in good faith believes the rule does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to State laws — limited preemption
rubrics_metrics.description: This part will not be construed to annul, or exempt any person from complying with any State statute, regulation, order, or interpretation applicable to a non‑compete clause, except that this part supersedes such laws to the extent, and only to the extent, that such laws would otherwise permit or authorize a person to engage in conduct that is an unfair method of competition under §910.2(a) or conflict with the notice requirement in §910.2(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.4(a); explains how the federal rule interacts with state law, including a limited preemption where state law would allow conduct the rule forbids or conflict with notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of State authority and private rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Except with respect to laws superseded under §910.4(a), no provision of this part shall be construed as altering, limiting, or affecting the authority of a State attorney general or any other regulatory or enforcement agency or entity or the rights of a person to bring a claim or regulatory action arising under any State statute, regulation, order, or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.4(b); preserves state enforcement authority and private rights to sue under state law except where expressly superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this part is held to be invalid or unenforceable by its terms, or as applied to any person or circumstance, the provision shall be construed so as to continue to give the maximum effect to the provision permitted by law and such invalidity shall not affect the application of the provision to other persons or circumstances or the validity or application of other provisions; any invalid provision or application shall be severable from this part and shall not affect the remainder thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.5; standard severability clause describing how remaining provisions remain effective if part is partially invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is §910.6; specifies when the rule's prohibitions and notice obligations become operative.
